extracted.intended_audience: general news audience and journalism/media professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing journalistic standards and verification practices applied to investigative audio journalism (podcasts), using the NYT 'Caliphate' investigation as an example. Focuses on verification, editorial oversight, fact-checking, corrections, and multimedia authentication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Firmer evidence required before publishing
rubrics_metrics.description: "In the absence of firmer evidence, 'Caliphate' should have been substantially revised to exclude the material related to Mr. Chaudhry."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not publish or center a narrative on claims unless there is firmer evidence to support them; where evidence is lacking, substantially revise or remove material tied to unverified claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work harder to verify claims
rubrics_metrics.description: "The newspaper said Friday it should have worked harder to verify the claims before deciding to make Chaudhry a central character."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply thorough verification steps before making a source a central narrative element; additional investigation and corroboration are required when making high-stakes factual claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require corroboration of essential aspects
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists were criticized as being "dismissive of the lack of corroboration of essential aspects" of Chaudhry's story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essential factual elements of a narrative must be corroborated by independent evidence or sources; lack of corroboration should prevent presentation as fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid making an unverified individual the central narrative character
rubrics_metrics.description: "The podcast as a whole should not have been produced with Mr. Chaudhry as a central narrative character."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrative structure should not hinge on a single source whose claims cannot be verified; balance storytelling with verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Involve an editor experienced in the subject matter from the start
rubrics_metrics.description: The Times said it "should have had an editor experienced in the subject matter involved in the series from the start."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign subject-matter-expert editors early in the project to oversee sourcing, verification, and context, especially for specialized beats like terrorism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous editing and fact-checking at all stages
rubrics_metrics.description: AP statement: her reporting "went through a rigorous editing process at all stages of the reporting and prior to publication. We stand by the stories."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement a rigorous, multi-stage editing and fact-checking workflow prior to publication or broadcast; document checks and corroboration steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply the same journalistic rigor to audio as to text
rubrics_metrics.description: The episode raises questions about whether the Times' audio unit "is set up to apply the same journalistic rigor to stories that the text version of the newspaper does."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audio production units must adopt the same verification standards, editorial processes, and oversight used for print/online text reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be skeptical when discrepancies appear and pursue follow-up
rubrics_metrics.description: An episode of "Caliphate" was devoted to discrepancies in his story and its own fact-checking, yet further verification was judged insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When discrepancies arise, increase skepticism and pursue deeper follow-up reporting rather than treating discrepancies as resolved; reassess reliance on the source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticate multimedia evidence (photos, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators found that Chaudhry had passed along photos taken by others in Syria as his own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify provenance and authorship of photos, videos, and other multimedia evidence before attributing them to a source; use forensic checks and independent corroboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid credulous reporting about verification steps
rubrics_metrics.description: The Times said its journalists were "too credulous about the verification steps that were undertaken."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not accept verification claims at face value; critically evaluate the sufficiency and independence of verification steps and seek corroboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue corrections, take accountability, and reassign personnel where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: The newspaper said it was "correcting the record" and the main reporter "will remain with the newspaper but will be reassigned." Leaders said they "should take blame."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When failures occur, publicly correct the record, explain what went wrong, and take appropriate personnel or structural actions (reassignment, oversight changes) to restore trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider reputational consequences and awards reassessment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Peabody Awards jurors are discussing what to do about its honor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that failures of standards may prompt reassessment of awards and honors; organizations and juries may need to review honors granted for work later found flawed.
